links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT responses versus OrthoInfo and sixth-grade target
links.effect: Standard ChatGPT FK mean 14.3 vs OrthoInfo 10.33 (P=0.002); sixth-grade prompt FK mean 7.71, still above sixth grade.
links.quote: In addition, the average reading grade level of standard ChatGPT responses was markedly higher when compared with that of OrthoInfo (standard FK mean = 14.3, OrthoInfo FK mean = 10.33; P = 0.002).

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses
links.effect: Standard ChatGPT responses at FK grade 14.3, above average American reading level and above OrthoInfo (10.33); sixth-grade prompt gave 7.71 but reduced accuracy.
links.quote: Not only does this far surpass the average American reading level, but this reading level is also greater than what is presented online, showcased by its notable difference when compared with the reading level for OrthoInfo.

links.outcome: Accuracy and appropriateness when ChatGPT asked to respond at a sixth-grade reading level
links.effect: Sixth-grade responses less accurate (3.6±0.76 vs 4.7±0.47; P<0.001) and appropriate (3.7±0.98 vs 4.5±0.57; P<0.001) than standard, below the 4/5 adequacy cutoff.
links.quote: Despite being easier to read, sixth-grade level ChatGPT responses compromised on accuracy and appropriateness.

links.outcome: Response quality change between equivalent queries differing in requested literacy level
links.effect: Adding a sixth-grade qualifier lowered accuracy (3.6 vs 4.7) and appropriateness (3.7 vs 4.5); questions 3-6 fell below adequacy threshold.
links.quote: Upon prompting ChatGPT to respond at a sixth-grade level, a notable trend emerged.

links.outcome: ChatGPT accuracy and appropriateness rated by surgeons against OrthoInfo reference
links.effect: Standard responses accuracy 4.7±0.47 and appropriateness 4.5±0.57, above 4/5 cutoff but below OrthoInfo 5.0 (P=0.004; P=0.016); sixth-grade below cutoff.
links.quote: However, standard ChatGPT responses were less accurate (4.7 ± 0.47 vs. 5.0 ± 0.0; P = 0.004) and appropriate (4.5 ± 0.57 vs. 5.0 ± 0.0; P = 0.016) when compared with OrthoInfo responses.

links.outcome: Clinical knowledge appropriateness of ChatGPT answers on rotator cuff tear management
links.effect: Question 5 appropriateness 3.6/5; response failed to state tears cannot heal with conservative management and suggested ultrasonography therapy lacking evidence.
links.quote: Surgeons found this response to be more inappropriate due to its failure to specify the inability to heal a rotator cuff tear through conservative management alone.
